title: A Few Robots First: Staged Rollout, the Wave That Cannot See a Rare Fault, and Halting on Silence

questions.question: What is a staged rollout for?
options: To learn about a bad release from a few robots before it reaches all of them
To spread the download so the network is not overloaded
To give each site its own version
To test the signature on a few robots
questions.explanation: A fault that hits 300 of 1000 robots was stopped after 4 failures in a first wave of 10. Sent to all at once it failed on 300.

questions.question: A release fails on one robot in two hundred. What is the chance a canary of 10 robots sees it?
options: 39.4 percent
95 percent
0.5 percent, the fault's own rate
questions.explanation: The chance that none of ten is a bad robot is 0.995 to the tenth, 0.951. So the canary sees the fault about one time in twenty.

questions.question: How many robots must have the release for a 95 percent chance of seeing a fault in one robot in two hundred?
options: 10: a canary is enough
598, which is 60 percent of a fleet of 1000
questions.explanation: For 0.995 to the n to fall to 0.05, n has to be 598. For 99 percent it is 919. A staged rollout shows how large the net would have to be.

questions.question: Why did the rollout with a threshold of 5 percent reach the whole fleet with 5 failures in 1000?
options: The failed robots did not report
The canary wave was skipped
0.5 percent is below 5 percent at every wave: the threshold never fires for a rare fault
The threshold was applied to the wrong wave
questions.explanation: Five failures in a thousand is half a percent, never above 5 percent in any wave. A threshold of zero halts, but only when a wave happens to include a bad robot.

questions.question: With 45 percent of the fleet silent, why must the rollout halt?
options: Silent robots are counted as failed
A small wave is always halted
Halting is the default when in doubt
There is not enough news to say it is safe, and a robot that crashed into a failed update is a silent robot
questions.explanation: A robot that failed to boot the update cannot report. Counting only those that reported, the rollout looked clean and went to all 1000, 450 of them unheard from.

questions.question: What helps with a rare, severe fault, since a canary cannot see it?
options: A lower failure threshold
Tests on the variants that exist before release, more robots and more time, and the hazard log: it belongs there and not in the rollout
A faster rollout, to find it sooner
A smaller first wave
questions.explanation: A canary of ten sees a one in two hundred fault one time in twenty. If the fault is severe it has to be found before release and recorded as a hazard.
